pieces.text: Sal ammoniac, a rare mineral made up of ammonium chloride

, is usually found near the vents of active volcanos. To collect samples of sal ammoniac, geologists must work when the weather is dry. If rainwater falls on the sal ammoniac, the mineral quickly dissolves to form a solution of ammonium ions
. The process of forming the ions absorbs thermal energy from the surroundings and converts it to chemical energy.

contents.text: Once it dries, concrete is stronger and more durable than many other building materials. It is resistant to wind, water, and temperature extremes. Buildings made of concrete provide better fire resistance than those made of wood. Concrete buildings also offer excellent energy efficiency.

Today, concrete is the most widely used synthetic material on Earth. Concrete has created structures like the Hoover Dam, the Burj Khalifa, and the Sydney Opera House. It is used to build homes, commercial buildings, roads, bridges, and sidewalks.
